chapter.title: Chapter Eight: The Crown
chapter.subtitle: The Open belongs to the people who play it.
chapter.description: Cross the neighborhood, win the final and defend the Open as the rooftop changes owners.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: Championship day. Six circuit tables get you from the corner store to the roof. I'm your first, and I'm the last one who says anything nice to you.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I put arrows on the signs. Last time somebody qualified for a *laundromat*.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: Because you *asked* me to and I *didn't think about it*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I put them at *every* junction. I did *not* put them at the laundromat junction. I want that in the *record* before there's an *investigation*.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: Cracked Head cleared the morning circuit at six in the morning. Nobody was here at six in the morning. *(Beat.)* He was here at six in the *morning*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: He didn't sleep.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's not *my* information. *(Beat.)* That's a thing I *know* because I unlock this building and I saw a *light*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I'm helping with setup. Before anybody asks, no, I am not secretly in this bracket.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Hitting a nail badly.)* Nobody said *any*thing. You said a *whole thing* to a *room that hadn't started*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: That's a *technique*, Cornball.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, not making a thing of it.)* Champ. Grab that box.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Which box.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: The blue one. No — the *other* blue one. *(Beat.)* There's four and I moved 'em around at *five o'clock in the morning* like a *person*, and I have lost the *system*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: (Looking at him.) Are you — are you doing the chairs again?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I'm setting up *tables*, and the tables have *legs*, and the legs go in the *middle*, and the middle is a *design choice*, and I have made it *four times* and I *dislike it*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Passing, not stopping.)* He's been doing it since four. He moved a table at *four* and Woke up a man who worked that day.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: That's a *different* table.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It's the *same* table, Blue.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, deadpan, walking past with a hammer.)* He's got a *system* and it's *bad*, and I've watched him for *four days* and I have *chosen*, every single time, not to say *one thing*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Why not?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* 'Cause last time I said a thing, I got put on a *bench* for a *week*, and the *bit* wasn't even *good*, and I have *learned*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: The bit was fine.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: The bit was *structural*, and I *know* the difference, and *you* don't, and that's *why* I can't.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: First. Promoter's next, then Cornball, then cross to the Red Side court. *(Beat.)*And here — *(She hands over a pen, and a *second* pen, and a folded sheet.)* Both of those are for you. The second

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: one is *mine*, and I want it back.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Why?

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: Because I write the sheets, and the reason I write the sheets is because once, *four years ago*, nobody did, and there was a *funeral* with the wrong *name* on the program, and I have been

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: personally *insufferable* about administrative detail ever since. *(Beat.)*Sign both. Bring mine back. If the day goes wrong, the sheet survives the day, and if the sheet survives the day, then

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: *somebody* knows who was supposed to be here.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: That's a system.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: That's a *system*, champ. Get in.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: The arrows are *very* clear. I tested them on Blue.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You followed me to the *bathroom*, Cornball.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *Thoroughly* tested. *(Beat.)*There's one at the top of the roof stairs that just says "this way" and it took me *forty minutes* to work out which way, and I have left it, because a man should be

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: able to figure it out, and because *somebody's* got to be the guy who notices and *sometimes* that guy's just the guy with the *arrow*.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Second. Winner keeps moving toward the roof.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Did you get the owner on the phone?

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: I've called four times. He confirmed the booking and then he stopped picking up. *(Beat.)*That's the third time this year he's stopped picking up, and it *is* a pattern, and I'm not going to say

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: it out loud in a *queue* because a man can't get his arm broken on championship day.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: So we keep going.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: We keep going. People came to play. Nobody's going to be told tonight that the building is gone and then asked to go *home*. They've earned a *table*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You've posted a final order. What happens if the schedule changes?

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)**Good* question. *(And he actually stops and thinks about it, which is his whole gift.)*The Crown is the schedule. Whoever holds it decides who plays. *(Beat.)*The building is *not* the

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: schedule. The building is a *room* the schedule happens *in*. *(Beat, and he is genuinely working it out in front of everybody.)*If the owner sells the *room*, the *schedule* doesn't move. If he

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: sells the *tournament*, that's a different thing, and I'd have to look at the paper, and I *wrote* the paper.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(From the back.)* You wrote the paper.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: I wrote the *paper*, Red.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Then you *know* the paper.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(To the room.)* Somebody get me my binder.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Article two. *(Beat.)*"The Block Party Open is a schedule, not a location. The holder of the Crown may move the schedule to any address. Transfer of the *venue* does not transfer the *schedule*."

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*You wrote that in *March*.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: I wrote that in *March*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Why?

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Because Red asked me to.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I asked him in *March* and he wrote it down and *never told anybody*, and it has been in a binder for *four years* waiting for exactly tonight.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: So the Crown doesn't stop the sale.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: The Crown has *never* stopped the sale. That's what the Crown *is*. What the Crown stops is somebody *else* deciding. That's a *much* smaller thing and most people would take it and call it

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: nothing.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: It's not nothing.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: No. *(Beat.)* It's the *whole* thing, if you're the person who gives it a *name*.

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: Second. Cornball's your last stop here, then cross to Red's court. *(He pins it up. Everybody reads it.)**(Beat.)*The order's up. That's it. That's the whole day. Everything else that happens now

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: is a *thing that happens to* a schedule.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I'll take the scoreboards.

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: Thanks. Leave the entry sheet with me.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Yeah. *(Beat.)* Fair.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: *(Low, to the player.)*That's two sheets now. Mine and the posted one. Same names, same order. *(Beat.)*If these two don't match at the end of the day, that's a *fact*, and a *fact* is the only

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: thing on this island that's ever changed anybody's mind.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Who are you going to give the second one to?

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* The new owner. *(Beat.)* When he calls. He's buying a *building*, champ. Somebody's gotta make sure he gets a *schedule* with it.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Third match. *(Beat.)* Before we begin: the vending company refunded my three dollars.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That's good.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*It's in *credit*. *(Beat — and he says it like a man reading a verdict.)*It's a *credit*. For the *same machine*. It lives *in the machine's memory*. She has not *given me money*. She has

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *acknowledged a debt* and *kept it*, and I have been thinking about this for a *week* and I've got a whole *thing* about it.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: You've spent *seven weeks* getting back a drink you already had.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I *stood for something.*

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: You stood in a *sun* for a *week*, champ.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Can I ask what's in it now?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat — and he is genuinely uncertain, which is new.)*I don't know. That's the *thing*. That's what's been *doing* to me. For seven weeks it was a *mystery* and the mystery had a *name* and I was

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: in a *relationship* with it, and now she's given me *credit* and I still don't know what's in her.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: So you never found out.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*I never *wanted* to know. *(Beat.)*That's the *horrible* part and I've been carrying it around since *Tuesday*. A victory you win by *never opening* the thing is not a victory, champ,

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: it's a *schedule*, and I have recently become very *aware* of the word.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*No, that's — hold on. *(And he's serious, and he turns to the player.)*I did it on purpose. I want that on the record, because I put the *thing* in the *thing* in a *joke* and it's

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *true*, and I have been the funny one all *season*, and the funny one gets to keep things *unfinished* because a *finished* thing is a thing somebody can *disagree* with.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: There. *(Beat.)*Eleven plates, ten chairs, a letter every month since the second of March, and a *three-dollar receipt* in a *clipboard* that says *I was right about a machine*. *(Beat.)*That's a

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *record*, champ. That's a man's whole *life* in a folder and it's *four things* and *every one of them's* a thing somebody was *wrong* about.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You carried it for seven weeks.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Yeah. *(Beat.)*And I'm taking it home, and I'm not setting up, and I'm going to put it in a *drawer* with a *key* in it, and on a *Thursday* when there's *nothing on* I'm going to take it

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: out and look at it for *no reason*. *(Beat.)*That's the whole plan. That's the entire *rest* of it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: You win. Go to Red's court. *(Beat.)*And I'm taking the cooler home. That's — That's a *thing* I'm doing, so I'm *saying* it: I'm taking the cooler home. I'm not setting it up. I'm not doing a

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *flyer*. I've got a *credit* slip and a *corner of it* in a *clipboard* and no *inventory*, and a *cooler* full of *water* that a *man in a barn* was supposed to *call* me about.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: That's the end of Liquid Gold.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Yeah. That's the end of it. *(Beat.)*It was a *nine dollar* thing, champ, and it ran a *week*, and I put *nine hundred* flyers, and it was the *best* bad idea I ever had. *(Beat.)*I'm not

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *sad*. I'm just — *(Beat.)*— it was the only thing on this block that was *mine*, and now it isn't, and I don't know what I'll do on a *Thursday*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You could do the plates.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* The plates.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You already do the plates.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: ...Yeah. *(Beat.)* I guess I already do the plates.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Take the cooler up the roof for me. I can't carry it and my hands are *done*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Why?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: 'Cause I keep the receipts, champ, and I want somebody up there to have a *drink* that I *bought*, and if I hand it to a man who *isn't* a *business*, then it's just a *favour*, and a favour

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *lasts*. *(Beat.)*A price is a thing that *ends*. I've been selling at a loss for *two years* and it's the only thing I ever had that *didn't* end.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Fourth. I'm glad you made it over.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: He's filming the whole thing himself today. Apparently Snitch charges extra for a *beginning*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: He offered me a redemption package.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Did it include an apology, or was that downloadable content?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It was a *bundle*, and the bundle was cheaper than I'd like, and the *bundle* included a *thumbnail* with my face on it, which I *declined*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Mid-match, not looking up.)* Baby Momma.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Don't do that during a *match*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: You read the rest of them.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I read all of them.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* The third one. The one where he asks whether you want the *money*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I read it nine times.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: You never said.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* What was I supposed to say. "Red, I got the *other* one"?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You could have said *anything*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: If I'd said anything, Red, we'd have had a *conversation*, and I was not *ready* to have a *conversation*, and I have had *nine hundred* of them in *four years*, and I am not *tired* —

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(She places a card.)*— I am *sorting*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I stopped asking OG whether it was safe.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Placing a card.)* I know.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Because the answer was always going to be the same, and a same answer *twice* starts looking like a *policy*, and I could not be a person who follows a *policy* about my brother's wife.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I know that too.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*So I stopped asking. And then I started *not asking* about things I *actually needed to know*, and that took a *year*, and I want that on the record as a *thing I did* and not a *thing I

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: suffered*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Did he ever ask for a picture.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*The fourth one. *(Beat.)*It's in the *envelope*, and I didn't bring the envelope, and I have been *not bringing* it since *March*, and I am going to have to bring it, and it is going to

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: be *ruinous*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Placing a card.)* Ruinous is fine.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I know it's fine.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Placing a card.)* I want you to know that it *is* fine, and that I know it's *fine*, and that you have spent *four years* not knowing whether it was fine. That's the whole bill.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: That's four. You earned every one of them. *(Beat.)* Snitch's next, then Hooper, and then the roof. And the envelope's in my car.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Why'd you tell me?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Because you've been carrying things for nine weeks and nobody's carried one for you, and that's a *terrible* way to live, and you're going to hit a wall in about *October*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Not touching it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Already walking away.)* When you're ready.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Red.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Stopping.)

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* The fourth message is a *picture* of them *sitting down*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: It's *four* years old. It is a *picture of my four year old sitting down*, and he is *going to see it*, and I have spent four years being angry at a *man who doesn't know that a picture exists*,

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: and in about *two hours* he is going to be *on a roof* with me.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Are you asking me to not give it to him?

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: I'm asking you to give it to him at *nine fifteen at night*, at a *door*, on a *Tuesday*, when he has *nothing else on*. *(Beat.)*Not on a roof. Not in front of anybody. *(Beat.)*If I give him a

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: picture of my child *up there*, in *public*, at a *final*, then that picture becomes about the *tournament*, and it will be in *nine* videos by *midnight*, and my child will be a *thing that

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: happened on this block*, and I will not have that.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Nine fifteen. Tonight. At the door. He comes by himself. *(Beat.)*And the *syrup* goes on the *side* in a *little cup*, and if he walks in here without a *little cup*, then he wasn't listening,

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: and he can go home and try again.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Nine fifteen. *(Beat.)* I'll be in the car.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: You will *not* be in the car.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* ...Fine.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Red.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: I'll be in the car.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Almost fond, and it's the only warmth in the node.)* Good man. Bad liar.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Fifth match, live from the Red Side court. Today's stream is called "The People Who Built It."

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Stopping.)* I didn't think you'd actually use the title.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I tried my version. Auntie reported it as misleading.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It was called "Snitch Saves Everybody."

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I took the *note*. *(Beat.)* She wrote it on a *card* and *handed* it to me, and I've had it in my *pocket* for a *week*, and I've looked at it *once*, and once was *enough*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: What was wrong with it.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Instantly.)* It was *optimistic*.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Champ. Ready? I would like to *contribute* something besides *captions* today.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What'd you change?

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*The *titles*. Every card I've put up this season has got a *name* on it, and the *name* is usually *me*, and today the *title* is the *people*. *(Beat.)*That's the whole change. It's a

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *metadata* change. It's *nothing*, and it's *everything*, and my chat is going to *ruin* it within *nine minutes*.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Reading a phone, flatly, no bit.)*"why is this guy acting like he built this." *(Beat.)*He's right. That's a *fair* point and it's *been* on the page all season and I am going to *keep it* up

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: there. *(Beat.)*Anybody else want to say something about the people? We're *live*. *(Beat.)*Y'all can go. I'm not building a *coalition* down here, I'm just a man with a *title* I don't *deserve*

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: yet.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Not looking at him. Playing.)* Turn your channel to camera three for a second.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Why?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Because the cables are on my table and I need to know if the third one is the one you keep stepping on.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Off-camera.)* Third one. Yeah. That one's mine. I know. *(Beat.)* Why is it *always* the third one.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Because the first two are *attached* and the third one is *loose*, and you have never once *checked* whether it was loose.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That is a *profound* thing to say about a cable.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It's a cable.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: Fifth. Hooper's the last circuit table, then the roof.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Picking up the cables. He has already coiled them.)* You're carrying these up.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Already coiled them.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* ...You did.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(And she says the thing that ends a two-year argument in seven words.)* Thank you.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That sounded weird for both of us.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: It did.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Not turning around. He's still on the ladder.)* Champ. Come hold this end.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: What is it.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: Four folders. Since *February*. *(Beat.)* Memorial. Cake. *(Beat — and he says the third one flatly, and it costs him.)* Blue. Hand-shaking. Four million views.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You said you'd take those down.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I *did* take them down. I took them *off my channel* and I put them in a *drawer* in my *flat* and I have been *living* with them for *nine weeks*, and I told myself that was *deleting* them, and

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: it is not, it is a *drawer*, and I've got a *friend* who knows exactly what a *drawer* looks like, so I'm going to *stop*.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(To the player.)*Take it. Don't — I don't want you to *watch* me do it, it's a *bit* if anybody's watching. *(Beat.)*There's four hundred and six clips in there, and if you *ever* post one of

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: them I will come to your *house*, and I don't even know where you *live*, and I'll *find out*, because that's the *worst* thing about me.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Walking to the bin.)*For the *record*, I'm not deleting them. I'm *returning* them. *(Beat.)*Which is a *thing I read*, and a *thing I read* is a *thing I did in February*, and I have apparently

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: been running a *library* out of a *drawer*.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Not looking up.)* Two hundred and six.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Four hundred and six.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I said two hundred and six of them are *unwatched*.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: Yeah. *(Beat.)* Let's keep moving.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: It's a good stream.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It's a good stream. *(Beat.)* You know what's in it?

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Cable.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Cable, and a woman telling me about the *third* one, and about *nine hundred* of my own words. *(Beat.)*I've got two years of *me* on a *server* and that's the whole inventory, champ, and

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: if I get hit by a *car* tomorrow the internet's gonna have to *watch a man move a cable* and that's it. *(Beat.)*And that's *fine*. *(Beat.)*That's *fine*, actually. Somebody put the *name* of the

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *thing* in the *title* and the *thing* is a *man on a ladder* and I *am* the man on the ladder, and I've been selling the *ladder* for *six years* as a *siege engine*.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: `(to the camera)` Nine hours ago, if a person had asked me what my channel was *for*, I'd have had a *twelve-minute* answer. *(Beat.)* Now I know. It's for a *third cable*.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

phases.name: semifinal push
phases.description: At round 4, the opponent gains 1 Motion once.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: Last circuit match. Winner gets the final against Cracked Head.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: He's already on the roof. No changes to the opponent, no changes to the rules.

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: Good. *(Beat.)* I trained for this. And I'd like one part of this tournament to go the way the *flyer* said.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Which part.

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*The *nobody* part. *(Beat.)*Everybody's had a good day. Cornball got his nine dollars. Red got his *feed*. Snitch got a *title* he doesn't deserve. Church Auntie got a *chair*. And

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: somewhere tonight, a *woman* is putting a plate at a table for *two*, and a man is going to walk in there with a *little cup*, and none of that's got *anything to do with cards*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: So which part's the flyer part.

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)**Anybody.* *(Beat.)*Not "everybody plays." I heard Auntie say it. There's a *difference* and it's been wrong for *eleven years*, and tonight the *only* person who's gonna say it out loud

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: is a man with a *card* at a *table* and *no reason to be here*, and I'd like it to be in *this* match. *(Beat.)*I'd like somebody to win this the way a person who was never *going* to win anything

preDialogue.speaker: Hooper
preDialogue.text: wins one. I'd like it to be *ugly* and I'd like it to be *boring* and I'd like it to be a *completely unremarkable* result that *the flyer* was *right about*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, low, with the clipboard.)* He's asking you to *win badly*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I'm not going to win badly.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I *know*. *(Beat.)*And I want to be *very clear* that I *heard* him say it, and I am writing it down, and if you go out there and give him a *good game* — *(He stops. He looks at the board.)*—

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: then you are going to have won six out of six and a man on a *roof* is going to be a *stranger* to the *holder of the Crown*, and I have been a man on this block for *nine years* and I am telling

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: you: that is *a thing*. That is a *whole thing* that can *go wrong*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I'm not going to play badly for a *metaphor*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat — and he's relieved, and disappointed, and honest about both.)*Yeah. Okay. *(Beat.)*That's the right *answer*, and it's also the *most* Block Party answer available, and I *hate* it,

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: because I have wanted a *stranger* to beat Cracked Head since about *eleven o'clock this morning* and I have *no evidence*.

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: You got me. *(Beat.)* Go finish it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: That was the best game of the day.

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It was the best game of *my* life and I lost it. Thank you. For making it a *game* and not a *qualification*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: That's the flyer part.

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: Yeah. *(Beat.)* That's about the size of it.

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: *(Coiling his deck, not looking at anybody.)* One more thing and then I'll get out of everybody's way.

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: I've watched that man work. Every morning, six in the morning, for *four years*, on a block where nobody asked him to. And I've watched *two* brothers try to hold a thing together, and I've

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: watched a woman *hold the actual thing*, and I've watched a *fifth* man hold a *clipboard* like it was a *lifetime job*, and not one of them — *(Beat)*— not one of them has ever once been *asked*

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: to be there by anybody in authority. There's no *job*. There's no *payroll*. Somebody just *keeps coming*.

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's the flyer part, champ. Not that anybody can play. That somebody can just *keep coming*. *(He stands.)* Don't make a speech on the roof. That's all I wanted. Don't make a speech.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I wasn't going to.

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah. I heard. *(He walks. Then, at the stairs:)* There's an arrow on that sign that only says "this way." I watched you look at it for eleven seconds.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I did.

postDialogue.speaker: Hooper
postDialogue.text: *(Without turning around.)* Good. *(Beat.)* That's the one that'll matter.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Final doesn't start yet. I've got a spare table if you want to keep your hands warm.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Play him. He's been moving chairs for two hours out of *nerves*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: They're better this way.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: You've changed them six times. Sit down before you find a seventh.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Looking at it.)* That's — *(Beat.)* That's the *one* from the *cocktail* table.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I kept it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: For *why*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Sitting.)*Because in nine weeks you have never once mentioned it, and you're a man who mentions *everything*, and I've been waiting to see whether it was going to come up. *(Beat.)*It didn't. So

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: it's still the joke.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Put it back.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: No.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Champ. Just a warm-up. You've already got the final. I can't take it off you even if I win, so let's take the *pretence* off the match.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You arranged this.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I arranged *this*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You know what I got wrong? And I want to say it up here, where the *table's* set up, because I'm not saying it at the *porch* and I'm not saying it at the *bar*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Blue—

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I thought if I was *good enough*, and I was *there*, then somebody'd *ask me* to carry something. *(Beat.)*And I have been *here* every single day since March, and nobody has *asked me* to carry a

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *single* thing. *(Beat.)*And that's not — *(Beat.)*— that's not a *reward* problem. That's a *thing I did*. Because if you *want* to be asked, then you've made yourself a *person who wants*, and

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: my father says that's the same as being a *person who didn't*, and he says that about *himself*, and he has *never once* said it about *me*, and I have spent *four years* being furious about which

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: one of us he thinks *worse* of.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Blue. I asked you to carry the *plates* on Tuesday.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I went back.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: To the nail tech.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Wednesday. I went back and I sat in the *chair* and I watched her do a *sleeve*.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Your sleeve.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *My* sleeve. Four years. It was still *going*. The cheap thread, from when I was — *(Beat.)* From when I was *nine*. It was still *going* in *January*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: She charged me fifteen. I gave her a hundred and she pushed it back and said I didn't get to *overpay* because then it'd be a *transaction*, and it *wasn't* one. *(Beat.)*So I sat there for an

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: hour and a half and she did a sleeve on a *nine-year-old's* coat and she *talked the whole time*, and champ — she told me about a *man* on Eleventh Street who owed her for a *hem*, and he's

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *still* owed, and she keeps the *ticket*, and she *waited*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: She keeps the tickets.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: She keeps the *tickets*. *(Beat.)*That's the whole thing, isn't it. She keeps the *ticket* and she *waits*, and the *waiting* is the *business*, and nobody ever *thanks* her for the *waiting*

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: because a ticket's just a *receipt*.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Blue. What did she say when you left.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* She said "same sleeve next time."

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* She said *next time*. *(Beat.)* I've been *four years* late, and she was *never* out of *tickets*, and she was *waiting*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat — and he can barely do it, and he does it anyway.)* Take your time. I'll show you.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Blue. It's nine fifteen.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(He looks at the light.)* Then that's now.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: My turn. I spent most of the season having conversations while somebody else played.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: I'll leave you to it.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: No. Stay.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Placing a card, not looking up.)* Red's got an envelope in his car.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I know.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: It's got a picture in it. It's four years old.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Okay.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: That's the *only* sentence I'm going to say about it tonight, and I said it, and now we're playing.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Good match. Go get him. *(Beat.)* He still thinks everybody's scared of that opening hand.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I'm standing right here.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Isn't that nice. Being here for what people say about you.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: You. Come here.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Yeah.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Nine fifteen. My door. He comes *by himself* — no you, no Red, no Snitch, no *camera*, and if I see a *phone* in that *doorway* I will end this and he can try again in a *year*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Baby Momma—

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: I'm not finished. *(To the player.)*And you're not coming. That's the *third* thing and I want it *understood*, because Red is going to try to *organize* this and he is going to offer to *drive*,

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: and I need you to say no to him before he *asks*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I'll say no.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Why?

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Because you'd be at the door in a *car* with a *bag* if I didn't.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah. That's why. *(Beat.)* Thank you.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Breakfast. Tomorrow. Seven thirty. You come to the *door* by yourself.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Seven thirty.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: And you will have something in your hand that has nothing to do with cards and nothing to do with money. Nothing in a bag, nothing in a box, nothing you'd have to *explain*. *(Beat.)*If you turn

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: up with a *present* I will know that you *think* you're sorry, and I am not asking you to be sorry, I am asking you to have *thought about it*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: The pancakes we talked about. No syrup on them. Little cup on the side.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat. Beat. Beat. Beat.)* You remembered.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I remembered.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(And she is not crying, and she is crying.)* Then —

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: And one more thing, and I'm telling you *now* so nobody can say I moved the goalposts. *(Beat.)*Red's bringing a picture. It's a photograph of them sitting down. *(Beat.)*He hands it to you and he

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: doesn't *say* what it is, and I am not going to tell you, and the reason I am not going to tell you is that I have been waiting *since April* to find out whether you took the *shortcut* or not.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I had this since May.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Who wrote it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: The *champion* wrote it. In a *courtyard*. I asked for a *memory* and a stranger gave me a *note*, and I have been *ashamed of that* for *three months*, and I have used it *every single morning*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat. Beat. Beat. Beat. Beat.)* You were *ashamed* of it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Every morning.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: And did it work.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I got here at seven twenty-two every morning for eleven days and I don't think a single one of them *drove*, and my *coat*'s the *right* one now, and — Yeah. It worked.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Then you'll do it without it. *(Beat.)* Throw it away.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Beat.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: You don't get to keep my kid's breakfast on a *napkin* for the rest of your life. You get to *remember* it, and remembering is a *thing you do* and not a *thing you carry*, and I have been

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *carrying* things on this island since the *second of March* and it has not *worked once*. *(Beat.)*So you throw it away, and in a *year* you either *remember* it or you don't, and if you don't,

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: then we'll *know*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(And she is not crying, and she is crying.)*Then go and *win* one, and don't do a *thing* with your face, because everybody up there is going to be *watching* you and I don't want a single one of

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: them to think this was *staged*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: What do you need tonight.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Not looking at him.)*Nothing. *(Beat.)*That's the *first* night in four years I've needed nothing, and I'd like it *noted*, and I'd like you to *not make it a thing*, and then I want you to go

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: up there and *win* and *not make a thing* about that either.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: And champ? When he gets there at half seven — *(Beat.)* — he won't need anybody. But he'll walk past this spot on the way up the stairs, and there's a thing I want him to see.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(To Red, low.)* You said you had a page.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Not turning.)* I did.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I've had it since April. I never opened it. *(Beat.)* I'm opening it now, in front of everybody, because I'm not going to walk around a season holding it and not look.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Reading, quietly.)* Third of March. *(Beat.)* Eleventh of March. *(Beat, and he stops.)* April. *(Beat.)* ...There's *one* in every month. *(Beat — and he puts it down.)* You made *twelve*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Not turning.)* Sixteen. There's sixteen. The last one's dated the *day you moved it*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* What do I owe you.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Flat, and everybody hears it, and the roof hears it.)* Not *that*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: I'm not going to burn it. Burning it is a *thing* that people do in *films*. *(Beat.)*I'm going to put it in the *same drawer* as the *tape*, and one day one of us is going to open that drawer and

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: be *furious*, and the other one is going to say "yeah, and it's *four hundred letters* too," and then *neither of us* will have to be *noble* about a *single* thing ever again.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Aunty counts eleven.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Very quietly.)* I know she does.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: How many is eleven.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Eleven plates, ten chairs, and a letter every *month* since the *second of March*, in a drawer in my *kitchen*, addressed to a man at an address I *had*. *(Beat.)*The *twelfth* letter

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: went out the week I stopped. *(Beat — and she is not crying and she is completely still.)*I put the twelfth one in the *oven*. It was a birthday card. *(Beat.)*I have never told a single person on

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: this island that and I am telling *four* of you on a *roof* at nine o'clock at night, and I would like the record to show that I said it *out loud* and that *nobody* is allowed to be *kind* about

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(From the stairs, not coming down.)*I'm not gonna be kind about it. *(Beat.)*I'm gonna be *specific*, 'cause that's my *job*. *(Beat.)*Your kid is *four* years old. That's eleven birthdays he's

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *missed*, and one that's in an *oven*, and every single one of them is a *card* that somebody *answered*, and that's not a *grief*, ma'am. That's a *person*. You've been answering mail for *four

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: years* on behalf of a *man who was alive*, and nobody in this *season* has said that out loud but *me*, so I'm saying it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: What thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: A clipboard. With a sheet on it, and eleven *names* on it, and a line through the *tenth* one, and nothing written on the *eleventh*. *(Beat.)*It's Cornball's. He leaves it here every night. He

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: thinks nobody looks at it.

phases.name: old claim
phases.description: At round 1, the opponent gains 1 Motion once.

phases.name: family pressure
phases.description: At round 3, the opponent gains 1 Motion once.

phases.name: open future
phases.description: At round 5, the opponent gains 1 Motion once.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: *(At the bottom of the stairs, not coming up.)*I'm going to say the part that belongs to me from down here, and then I'm going up the *other* set of stairs and I am not coming back up this one.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Final table. Tonight's champion against the man who held the title before he went missing. The rules are the same ones we started with. Go.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* First night back, I thought beating you would make everything feel like it used to.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Did it?

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*No. *(Beat.)*It made me *feel* like it used to, which is worse, because you can *train* for that, and then you win and you're *still hungry*, and there's nobody in the *world* who can

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *help* with that.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You told me to hold being angry with my brother and playing this at the same time.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I did.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*I want you to know that I *hate* that it worked. *(Beat.)*I've been angry with him for eleven days and I played a *perfect game* this morning and I was *angry* the entire time, and I

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: could *feel* the other thing at the same time, and *that's* your fault, and I want *credit* for doing it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You get the credit.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: You kept showing up. Through all our *bullshit*. *(Beat.)*You never had a *side*. You never did a *thing* for your own *position*. I asked you, on the second night, what your *angle* was, and you

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: said you didn't have one, and I thought that was *naive*, and then I watched you for nine weeks.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I asked you the same thing once. In *week one*. You said you were here for a *chair*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I was.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Yeah. I asked you the same thing in *week one* and I wanted to hear something about *me*. I asked *twenty* people in *week one* and I wanted to hear something about *me*, and I never once

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: said so.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Then sit down.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I'm sitting.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: You earned this table. Now I want to see if I can earn the seat across from you.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Let him have it. He's the guy who noticed.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That's mine.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Yeah. It is. *(Beat.)* It was never going to be anybody's, champ. It was only ever going to be a *thing somebody else had to hand over*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: THAT'S OUR WINNER! Somebody get a *photograph* before he asks for a *rematch*!

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I was going to ask next week.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: He's going to ask *next week*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Not to anybody.)* I've never looked at this.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Coming over.)* Red.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: I've moved it eleven times. I knew what page it was on. I knew it was the *back*. I never once *turned to it*, and I've been carrying a *thing I won't look at* around this island for four years,

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: and I want to be *very clear* that I did not know that was what I was doing until just now.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* He wrote his *scores* in it. *(Beat.)* In the back. In *pen*. Like a *child*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* How many.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Two years of them. *(Beat.)* Every Sunday. *Every one.*

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Long beat.)* He's still playing.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* What?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: He's *still playing*, Red. He's *twenty* pages into a *second run* of this. I don't know who he's winning for. I don't know who's *writing* on the other side. *(Beat.)*But he's still *keeping

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: score*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Four years, and I never once opened a *binder*. I *yelled* at a *room*, every week, for *four years*, and there was a *book* about forty feet away that would have told me he was *writing*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You want to hold it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* No. If I hold it, I turn it into something about *me*, and I've done that four times.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Put it in the binder for the *Open*. Article two's in there, isn't it. Put it *next to* Article two. *(Beat.)*So the next person who reads the *rules* has to see a *man writing his own scores* on

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: the way past.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's the least dramatic place on this island.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yes. And he'll still read it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Closing it.)*Forty years of Sundays on this island and it was *never* in a *drawer*. *(Beat.)*I put it there. On a *Tuesday*, in *March*, in about *four minutes*, because I didn't know what else

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: to do with my *hands*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Red. Is his *name* in it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It's his binder too. I never *owned* it. I've just been the *librarian*.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Handing over two folded sheets. Hers and Bottle Girl's.)* Same names, same order. *(Beat.)* That's two people, and one of them doesn't know you exist, and she kept it *anyway*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: What happens when he calls.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Beat — and she looks at the roof, at the light, at the whole block.)*Then you hand him *this*, and you say *anybody can play*, and you find out what his *number* is. *(Beat.)*And whatever his

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: number is, you say it *out loud*, in front of a *witness*, on a *Tuesday*. *(Beat.)*That's the whole job. That's what I do, and I've been doing it for *four years*, and I'm *handing it over*, and

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I'd like you to understand that I'm handing it over because it is *late* and I am *tired*, and not because you *won*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: There's no neutral.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* No. *(Beat.)* There really isn't.

tips: Continue the story at your own pace.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: Winner sits. Everybody else helps. That is the seating plan and it is not open to appeal.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: I brought drinks. From a store. Handed to me by a person with a job and a name and a whole life.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Put them here. *(He takes two, sets them down, moves a chair, moves it back.)* Baby Momma, the extra cups are under the sink.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I know where they are. I've known where they are for four years.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Both my sons carrying plates. *(Beat.)* I ought to charge admission.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: You should have started with the yard sale, Dad. You'd have made more.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: *(He doesn't laugh. He almost does.)* I'd have had to look at people.

scenes.speaker: Delivery Demon
scenes.text: Promoter? Sorry. Signed notice. He wanted it delivered while everybody was in one place.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Read it.

scenes.speaker: Delivery Demon
scenes.text: "To the tenants of 1140. The premises are sold. Transfer effective the first of the month. The new owner will be in contact regarding scheduling and access."

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: He's done. He actually did it.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Weeks. It took us *weeks* to get everybody back up there, and he sells it out from under a dinner table.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: Read the rest before you climb on that roof.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: What does "the new owner will be in contact" mean. What would you have to say to someone to get that sentence.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: *(He reads it again.)* It means the owner told him to figure out what the block was before he priced it. It's not a letter. It's a question he already asked himself.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: It's a *broadcast*. *(Nobody looks at him.)* Okay. But somebody should be saying out loud, on the record, that Techbro Rich did not buy a tournament, he bought a parking lot with people in it.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Then I'll be the one who talks to him.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: With respect, champ. You've been here eight weeks. He's got a lawyer.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: I've got the Open. *(Beat.)*The Crown isn't a trophy, it's the schedule. Whoever holds it sets who's allowed to play. That's not a thing a landlord can override, because he doesn't own the league,

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: he owns the *roof*, and we're not on his roof unless he kicks us off, and if he kicks us off then he just bought an empty building and the tournament is somebody else's problem, and it stops

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: mattering who's on the roof.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: That's actually true.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* It's true and it's also the only card anybody in this room has ever held. Nobody's used it before because nobody's ever gotten that far without owing somebody something for it.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Then you'd be walking into that meeting as a brand-new champion with a rulebook and nothing behind it. He could just... not answer.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: I know. But every one of you is about to tell him your name is on a piece of paper he didn't sign. I'm the only one walking in there with nothing to lose and a rule that already exists. Let me be

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: the one.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Do it.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Dad—

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I have got maybe a year, Blue. I have been sitting in this chair since you were both small, and I have never once in this family been the person who said *go*. I am saying it. Let them go.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: *(He pulls out a phone, then puts it back, then pulls it out again.)* So what do I tell them.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Tell them the Open is under the same rules. Open entry, no side colors, no charge. If Rich wants the roof, he rents it to us at the same rate the last four years ran, and the schedule stays mine.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: What if he says no.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Then we play somewhere that isn't his. Corner store's got a lot of folding chairs and nobody's been using that lot since the laundromat closed.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(He has gone very still.)* Champ. Did you just say corner store.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: I said corner store.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: I'm going to need a minute.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Already standing, already collecting plates.)*Everybody's got a rooftop to lock up. Rich can have the building at nine in the morning. He can have it in the dark, he can have it while he's

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: eating, he can have it in a paper bag, and he cannot have it with my table still set up on it.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: *(To nobody.)* For the record, I'd stream this if anybody let me. But nobody's letting me, and that's — *(Beat.)* — that's actually the correct call, and I want it noted that I said so.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Champ. You don't have to be here at seven to meet him.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: I'll be there at six-thirty.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Six-thirty.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: *(He stops in the doorway with the chairs.)* I know what you did tonight. I want to say that before I go up the stairs and pretend I'm not thinking about it.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: You don't have to.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: I know I don't. That's why I'm saying it. *(He doesn't put the chairs down.)* Seven-thirty tomorrow. Not my thing. Somebody else's.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Go on.
